title: Human Resource Management Adventure 1: Motivation Theories
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Maslow, Herzberg, McGregor and McClelland — the four giants of motivation.
meta_desc: Business Management HRM: Maslow's hierarchy, Herzberg's two-factor, McGregor X/Y, McClelland's needs.
final_note: You compared four motivation theories and applied each to the workplace.

concepts.def: McGregor: workers are lazy and need control
McGregor: workers are self-motivated and creative

walkthroughs.body_html:
Abraham Maslow (1943) proposed five needs in ascending order.

1. Physiological — food, shelter (basic wage).
2. Safety — job security, safe site.
3. Social — belonging, teams.
4. Esteem — status, recognition.
5. Self-actualisation — fulfilling potential.

A need only motivates while unmet; satisfied needs lose pull.

Frederick Herzberg (1959) found that hygiene factors (pay, conditions, supervision) prevent dissatisfaction but do not motivate.

True motivators are intrinsic: achievement, recognition, the work itself, responsibility, advancement.

Implication: raising wages stops complaints but won't drive effort — job enrichment will.

Douglas McGregor (1960): Theory X managers see staff as lazy and use control; Theory Y managers see staff as ambitious and delegate.

David McClelland (1961): people are driven by three learned needs — nAch (achievement), nAff (affiliation), nPow (power) — in different mixes.
